A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IF-RewardBench study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G are readable and can be matched despite reflow and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of 21 judge models, human comparisons, inference-time scaling experiments, and downstream Best-of-8 evaluation on 300 instructions.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical studies and adds evaluation results for another reward model in Table 4.

M1.justification: Preference-graph construction, Pareto-based preferences, constraint scoring, and pairwise-to-Elo ranking remain unchanged. The new checklist-revision guidelines document the manual revision step already described in v1 Section 3.2.1.

E1.justification: Both retain 842 instructions, 6,011 responses, the same three instruction types and source benchmarks, and the 300-instruction downstream evaluation. Real-world and synthesized instructions newly itemized in v2 Table 10 were already included in v1.

E2.justification: v2 adds Qwen2.5-Math-RM-72B to the overall-assessment comparison in Table 4, increasing the overall model roster from 21 to 22. The constraint-assessment and downstream-correlation comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The printed pairwise-comparison prompt adds a final-round user-instruction field absent from v1 Table 20 (v2 Table 21). This revises the documented evaluation input without establishing that experiments were rerun. Other stated metrics, sampling procedures, and decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The constraint-type and performance-factor analyses, thinking and self-consistency ablations, length analysis, and instruction-hierarchy case studies are retained in Figures 4–5, Table 5, and Appendices F/G.3.

E5.justification: Annotation agreement and Cohen's kappa reporting remain unchanged, including the statistics in Appendix E.3. v2 adds no run/seed information, uncertainty estimates, or statistical tests.

E6.justification: Table 4 adds Qwen2.5-Math-RM-72B Kendall correlations of 0.056 for single-turn, 0.092 for multi-turn, 0.002 for system-prompt, and 0.050 overall. Existing scores and findings are retained, including downstream results moved from v1 Table 12 to v2 Table 7.

T1.justification: The task definitions, constraint taxonomy, scoring equation, and Pareto-dominance conditions in Equations 1–3 remain unchanged. No new mathematical argument or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of broad instruction coverage, human-verified preference graphs, challenging judge evaluation, and stronger correlation with downstream performance. The additional evaluated model does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and limitations concerning language-specific performance and annotation subjectivity are retained. The added main-text statement about avoiding length bias repeats the interpretation already present in v1 Appendix F.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents per-source instruction counts in Table 10, seed provenance and difficulty-based selection in Appendix B.2, and checklist-revision procedures in Appendix E.1/Table 15. It also completes the printed pairwise prompt. These additions improve documentation without establishing reconstruction of the dataset.

R1.justification: v2 adds Yang et al. (2024b), the Qwen2.5-Math technical report, alongside the additional reward model. The related-work discussion and substantive research positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are limited wording corrections, expanded explanations in Appendices B.2/E.1, and a new Acknowledgments section. Limitations becomes unnumbered, while the main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds checklist-guideline Table 15, expands the source table with separate rows and counts, and relocates downstream results from Table 12 to Table 7. Table sizing, prompt formatting, spacing, and page-number footers change; the existing figures are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves reproducibility through explicit source counts, checklist-revision instructions, and completion of the printed pairwise prompt. The additional reward-model result modestly broadens comparison. These are useful, limited gains: the benchmark design, existing findings, and limitations remain stable, and the PDFs do not establish a change to executed prompting.
